summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 10th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well, with mild transaminitis and manageable nausea and arthralgias that resolved within 24 hours. Methotrexate levels decreased appropriately by day three, allowing for safe discharge. She remained neurologically stable throughout the admission, with chronic right foot pain controlled on gabapentin. Her eosinophilia was noted but attributed to asthma and managed with montelukast. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to restart mesalamine, continue enoxaparin, and follow up with oncology in four weeks for her next cycle and MRI.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
